title: MASAI trial: AI-supported breast screening
what: The first randomised trial of AI-supported mammography screening, with about 106,000 women, found 12% fewer interval cancers than standard double reading. Earlier results showed 29% more cancers detected and 44% less reading work.
why: Fewer cancers missed between screenings, with less radiologist time per woman screened.

sources.title: AI support in breast cancer screening: Fewer missed cancer cases

title: C2S-Scale finds a way to make tumours more visible
what: A 27B-parameter open model built on Gemma simulated over 4,000 drugs and flagged silmitasertib as a 'conditional enhancer' that can make tumour cells more visible to the immune system. Lab tests in human cell models confirmed it.
why: An AI-generated cancer hypothesis that held up in the lab. Early-stage, preprint only, but real science.

sources.title: Google Deepmind's new Gemma model helped discover a new cancer treatment pathway

title: ArteraAI Prostate authorised by the FDA
what: The FDA granted De Novo authorisation to AI software that reads biopsy pathology images to estimate long-term outcomes, such as risk of metastasis, for patients with non-metastatic prostate cancer. Validated on data from phase 3 trials.
why: Helps decide who needs more aggressive treatment and who can be spared it.

sources.title: Artera Receives U.S. FDA De Novo Marketing Authorization for AI Digital Pathology Software Revolutionizing Prostate Cancer Care
FDA grants de novo authorization to ArteraAI Prostate

title: PRAIM: AI in Germany's breast screening programme
what: A real-world study of 463,094 women screened at 12 German sites found AI-supported reading detected 6.7 breast cancers per 1,000 versus 5.7 without AI, 17.6% more, with no increase in recall rate.
why: More cancers found in routine screening, without more false alarms.

sources.title: Nationwide real-world implementation of AI for cancer detection in population-based mammography screening

title: AlphaFold wins the Nobel Prize in Chemistry
what: Half of the 2024 Chemistry Nobel went to the creators of AlphaFold2, which predicts protein structures. In one early use, AlphaFold structures helped find a new inhibitor candidate for a liver cancer target, CDK20.
why: Knowing a protein's shape is a starting point for designing drugs against it, cancer drugs included.
